options.name: Lifestyle modification
options.population: All adults with elevated blood pressure or hypertension
options.summary: All three guideline-level sources place heart-healthy lifestyle change (diet, exercise) at the start of care. The 2024 ESC guidance advises it for everyone with elevated blood pressure and starts it alongside medication in hypertension; Hypertension Canada lists it among its treatment recommendations.

options.name: Antihypertensive drug therapy
options.population: Adults with hypertension (≥140/90 mm Hg), or ≥130/80 mm Hg at moderate-to-high risk after lifestyle change
options.summary: Medication is started together with lifestyle change at 140/90 mm Hg or more under the 2024 ESC guidance, and may be considered from 130/80 mm Hg in moderate-to-high-risk patients. Hypertension Canada gives stepwise medication guidance, and MedlinePlus notes some people need more than one type of medicine.

options.name: Intensive systolic target (below 130 mm Hg)
options.summary: The 2024 ESC guidance targets 120-129 mm Hg and Hypertension Canada (2025) targets below 130 mm Hg. A 2020 Cochrane review found that lower targets did not reduce total mortality or serious adverse events versus a standard target of 140/90 mm Hg or lower.

options.name: Blood pressure targets in older adults
options.population: Adults aged 60-65 years or older with hypertension
options.summary: The 2017 ACP/AAFP guideline targets a systolic pressure below 150 mm Hg for adults 60 or older, and below 140 mm Hg after stroke or TIA or at high cardiovascular risk. The 2024 Cochrane update found a target of 140/90 mm Hg or lower reduces stroke in adults 65 or older, and notes guideline targets range from below 130 to below 150 mm Hg.

options.name: Systolic target below 120 mm Hg in chronic kidney disease
options.population: Adults with chronic kidney disease not receiving dialysis
options.summary: KDIGO 2021 recommends a systolic target below 120 mm Hg for adults with CKD not on dialysis, stating that this differs from some other guidelines.

options.name: Standardized blood pressure measurement
options.population: Adults being diagnosed or treated for hypertension, including those with CKD
options.summary: Hypertension Canada and KDIGO both recommend a standardized approach to measuring blood pressure, used to confirm the diagnosis and to guide treatment.

options.name: Diuretics
options.population: Adults with hypertension starting first-line therapy
options.summary: In a 2022 Cochrane review of first-line therapy, diuretics reduced major cardiovascular events and congestive heart failure more than calcium channel blockers (moderate certainty).

options.name: Calcium channel blockers
options.population: Adults with hypertension starting first-line therapy
options.summary: First-line CCBs did not differ from other classes on all-cause mortality. They probably reduce major cardiovascular events more than beta-blockers but less than diuretics, and are the most-studied partner in single-pill combinations with ARBs.

options.name: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers
options.population: Adults with hypertension starting first-line therapy
options.summary: Compared with CCBs, ACE inhibitors and ARBs were associated with less congestive heart failure, while CCBs reduced stroke versus ACE inhibitors and myocardial infarction versus ARBs (low to moderate certainty).

options.name: Beta-blockers
options.population: Adults with hypertension starting first-line therapy
options.summary: As first-line therapy, beta-blockers were outperformed by CCBs on major cardiovascular events, stroke and cardiovascular mortality.

options.name: Single-pill combination therapy
options.population: Adults with hypertension needing two or more drugs
options.summary: Adherence and persistence are generally higher with single-pill than free-dose combinations, most often CCB/ARB pairs, but mostly observational evidence has not shown whether this improves BP control or cardiovascular outcomes.

options.name: Spironolactone for resistant hypertension
options.summary: The 2024 ESC guidance recommends spironolactone for resistant hypertension.

options.name: Renal denervation
options.summary: The 2024 ESC guidance names renal denervation as an alternative to adding further antihypertensive medication in resistant hypertension.

options.name: Treating the underlying cause of secondary hypertension
options.population: People whose high blood pressure is caused by another condition or a medicine
options.summary: MedlinePlus notes that treating the causative condition or stopping the causative medicine may lower blood pressure.
